question: What is another common name used for congenital anomalies?
explanation: Congenital anomalies are structural or functional abnormalities present from birth, commonly known as birth defects. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h1)

question: When can congenital anomalies typically be identified?

options.A: Only during the adolescent growth spurt
options.B: Strictly after fifty years of age
options.C: Before birth, at birth, or later in infancy

explanation: These conditions develop during fetal growth and may appear anytime from the prenatal period through early childhood. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h1)

question: Which maternal vitamin deficiency is strongly linked to neural tube defects?
explanation: Sufficient maternal folic acid intake before and during early pregnancy helps prevent neural tube defects. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h2)

question: A pregnant patient takes unregulated local herbal remedies. What primary risk does this pose to the fetus?

options.A: Exposure to potential teratogens affecting fetal development
options.B: Complete prevention of normal gestational diabetes
options.C: Immediate maternal kidney failure within twenty-four hours
options.D: Enhanced immunity against all congenital heart diseases

explanation: Herbal remedies taken during early pregnancy can act as teratogens and disrupt normal organ development. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h2)

question: Which condition is classified as a structural congenital anomaly?
explanation: Cleft lip is a visible physical malformation, placing it in the structural anomaly category. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h3)

question: How do functional anomalies generally differ from structural ones?

options.A: They only appear in adulthood after years of heavy manual labor
options.B: They cannot be diagnosed under any circumstances in a primary clinic
options.C: They never require medical intervention or lifelong dietary changes
options.D: They involve metabolic or physiological system disorders rather than visible malformations

explanation: Functional anomalies affect how body systems work chemically or biologically, often requiring special screening tests rather than a visual check. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h3)

question: A newborn presents with an open spina bifida sac. What is the immediate nursing action for the lesion?

options.A: Leave the defect completely open to dry in the room air
options.B: Cover the sac with sterile, warm, saline-soaked gauze
options.C: Apply dry cotton wool tightly across the exposed tissue
options.D: Massage the surrounding skin firmly to stimulate circulation

explanation: Sterile, saline-moistened dressings protect delicate exposed neural tissue from drying out and injury before surgery. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h4)

question: Why is keeping warm particularly important for a newborn with major structural defects?

options.A: Warm environments cause spinal openings to close spontaneously
options.B: Open defects and malformations increase the risk of rapid heat loss
options.C: Babies with anomalies do not have sweat glands at any age
options.D: Hypothermia completely cures congenital heart murmurs within hours

explanation: Compromised skin and open lesions make it harder for a newborn to maintain a normal body temperature. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h4)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary healthcare team essential for managing complex birth defects?

options.A: Specialists ensure that parents never experience grief or emotional distress
options.B: Different specialists address the diverse surgical, medical, and developmental needs of the child
options.C: Hospital administrative policies mandate that at least five doctors sign discharge forms
options.D: Single nurses are legally prohibited from touching infants with genetic disorders

explanation: Complex anomalies affect multiple body systems, requiring teamwork from various clinical specialists for the best care. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h5)

question: What primary emotional response do parents commonly exhibit after learning their baby has a birth defect?
explanation: The sudden realization of a birth defect often triggers intense emotional trauma, requiring sensitive nursing support. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T020#GNS226_U3_T020_h5)
